question: As per Human Development Index (HDI) 2025, what is the rank of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**130th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India has been ranked **130th** in the **Human Development Index (HDI)** for the year **2025**.
 
• The **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a composite statistical tool used to rank countries by level of "human development" and is released annually by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**.
 
• The ranking is based on a score that reflects achievements in key dimensions of human development, placing India within the **Medium Human Development** category among the **193 countries** and territories evaluated.
 
• The index considers several critical indicators, including **life expectancy at birth**, **expected years of schooling**, **mean years of schooling**, and **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita**.
 
• India's position at **130th** signifies the ongoing transition and progress in social and economic parameters, though it highlights the need for further improvements in healthcare and educational infrastructure compared to global leaders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dimensions of HDI:**
 
 
• **Long and Healthy Life**: This is measured by **Life Expectancy at Birth**. It reflects the overall health and quality of the medical system in a country.
 
• **Knowledge**: This dimension is measured by a combination of **Mean Years of Schooling** (for adults aged **25 years** and older) and **Expected Years of Schooling** (for children of school-entering age).
 
• **Decent Standard of Living**: This is measured by **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita** adjusted for **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)** in **US Dollars**.
 
 
 
• **The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**:
 
 
• The **UNDP** was formed on **November 22, 1965**, and is headquartered in **New York City**. It is the leading agency of the **United Nations** focused on international development.
 
• The **Human Development Report (HDR)** has been published by the **UNDP** since **1990** to emphasize that people and their capabilities should be the ultimate criteria for assessing the development of a country.
 
 
 
• **Scoring System**:
 
 
• The **HDI** value ranges between **0 and 1**. Countries with a score of **0.800** or above are categorized as **Very High Human Development**, while those below **0.550** are categorized as **Low Human Development**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Origin of HDI**: The index was created by **Pakistani economist Mahbub ul Haq** and **Indian economist Amartya Sen** in **1990** to shift the focus of development economics from national income accounting to people-centered policies.
 
• **Complementary Indices**: The **HDR** also features other indices such as the **Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI)**, the **Gender Development Index (GDI)**, the **Gender Inequality Index (GII)**, and the **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**.
 
• **India's Historical Trend**: Since **1990**, India's **HDI value** has shown a consistent upward trend, largely driven by significant increases in **life expectancy** and **GNI per capita**, despite periodic fluctuations in global rankings.
